fun_highlights: The vocation fork (soldier / scholar / maker / wanderer) is a genuine structural divergence — a soldier life really does hit different cards (a_soldier_service, m_soldier_ghost, vx_soldier_war) than a scholar life (a_scholar_question, m_scholar_legacy, e_scholar_old), and when those collide with an era (vx_scholar_turning, vx_soldier_war) the intersection produces content that exists nowhere else. That is the design working.

Era rotation gives each dynasty its own weather. Dynasty 2 has war framing the calling choice at 14 ('There is a war on, and it is hungry for the young'). Dynasty 7 opens in hard years ('lean time'). Dynasty 6 becomes an artistic house because of accumulated rep, not a scripted beat. These feel like different worlds, not reskins.

Callback cards genuinely pay off. The 'looked away' arc fires in Tamsin (Dynasty 2) twice: once she redeems it, once she doesn't — and both are poignant. The 'cb_books_late' circle closing in Rafael (Dynasty 7) at age 54 reading the childhood book is the best example of the system doing what it promises. When these land, they feel earned and irreplaceable.

Life-shape diversity is real in the transcripts. Dynasty 2 (Tamsin): solitary scholar ending 'with the plain ache of it.' Dynasty 8 (Esme): wanderer who settles, frail, no heir. Dynasty 9 gen 3 (Otto Halloran): solitary maker who finds love late and dies without a direct heir — the house passes sideways. Dynasty 6 gen 5 (Emory): born rich, never struggles, faces different pressure cards (s_great_burden, s_patronage). These are genuinely different life-shapes, not the same arc re-labelled.

Dynasty-memory cards (d_ancestor, d_motto_test) create a living continuity. When Caleb (Dynasty 6 gen 4) is tested against the family motto 'Beauty is the only argument we trust' at age 27, and then Lucan (Dynasty 4 gen 5) breaks with his at 62, the same structural card produces opposite emotional notes. That is re-use that earns its keep.

The collateral succession mechanic allows a genuinely childless solitary arc to not be a dead-end, which breaks the old domestic monoculture without erasing stakes. Seeing 'the name passes sideways, to one of the wider family' in Bjornsen gen 3 (Naima, no heir) and Mercer gen 3 (no direct heir) while the house persists opens up solitary and childless shapes as viable and distinct.
staleness: The childhood beat-order is still recognisably invariant in practice. Across the 15 dynasties I can identify in the transcripts, nearly every childhood opens with c_origin at 3-5, then clusters around c_friend/c_sick/c_dark/c_wonder within a few years of each other. The trait-affinity weighting (bookish toward c_book, warm toward c_friend) theoretically diverges these, but in the actual transcripts the visual rhythm of childhood reads as interchangeable: origin card → 1-2 flavour cards → calling at 14-20. Greta (Dynasty 5) has c_unfair at 7, c_wonder at 9, c_grandparent at 11, then calling at 14. Cleo (Dynasty 9 gen 2) has c_wonder at 11. Carys (Dynasty 4 gen 3) has c_sibling at 7, c_talent at 11. The specific cards vary; the structural feel of a 3-card childhood checklist does not.

The love/marriage/child cluster repeats at a level that still registers as sameness across a session. Every dynasty-continuing life in the transcripts includes: fell in love → 'meet them halfway' (or late love) → marriage prompt → child prompt. The text rotates well ('Married Matthias young and spent the years proving it had not been rash' vs. 'Married Beatrix. The day was small and the meaning was not.'), but the structural beat — love arrives, marriage is posed, child is posed — lands in every domestic life at roughly adult-entry, mid-adult, late-adult. By dynasty 8 a variety-seeker reads the marriage prompt as a genre obligation rather than a moment of genuine choice.

Once-per-dynasty (onceDyn) cards thin the pool for later generations. By generation 4 or 5 of a long dynasty (Bjornsen runs 5 generations, Quint runs 5), the already-seen-dynasty cards have burned: s_from_nothing, m_peer_dies, t_warm, d_ancestor, e_legacy, e_bequest, cb_reckless, etc. Lucan (Bjornsen gen 5) and Emory (Quint gen 5) get noticeably shorter transcripts — not because they die young, but because the pool has thinned. A variety-seeker playing a long dynasty will feel the well running dry by gen 4.

The 'competing goods' and 'dilemma' cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty, x_promise, x_mercy, x_favour) are structurally near-identical: two named virtues, choose between them, quiet aftermath. The writing is excellent but the grammar is so consistent that by the third time the player recognises 'two-virtue fork, no clean answer' as a card type rather than a new situation. Seen in Tamsin (x_promise), Cleo Bjornsen (x_loyalty_truth), Greta (x_honest_or_kind implicit), Naima (x_promise), Vera (t_shrewd). The writing distinguishes them; the felt texture does not.

Fate cards (f_fire, f_sudden_loss, f_grace, f_reversal) are once-per-life and cooldown-blocked, so they fire at most once each. But f_grace and f_reversal have exactly one choice option (no real decision — just 'take what happened'), which means when one lands, the moment is purely observational with no player agency. In a game built on meaningful choices, a no-choice fate card feels like padding rather than punctuation.

The elder stage still converges on a recognisable beat-cluster. Every elder life runs at least two of: m_health / e_body → parent dies → e_garden or e_last_walk → e_legacy or e_bequest → e_peace or e_solitary. The prose is varied; the sequence isn't. By dynasty 6 I can anticipate the elder section's shape before the character reaches 60.

improvements.what: Break the childhood three-card checklist by gating more childhood cards on ERA, SEAT, or SPECIFIC TRAIT combinations rather than just broad age windows. For example: a war-era child should almost never get c_wonder (who stops to contemplate flowers with war in the air?), but should see c_dark and c_unfair more. A seat-5+ born child should get different childhood texture than a seat-0 child — the code has c_origin's text branching on seat/era, but the subsequent childhood cards mostly don't. Two more seat/era-specific childhood variants would make each era's childhood feel lived-in, not just differently labelled.
improvements.why: The childhood stage is the most repeated structural phase across all fifteen dynasties in the transcripts. Even a variety-seeker who chooses differently each time sees the same 3-card rhythm. Era-gating the pool breaks this without requiring new card volume.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 mid-adult 'intersection' cards that exist ONLY at the cross of a vocation AND a specific era AND a dynasty condition (e.g., a scholar in a plague era must grapple with whether to keep studying or go tend the sick; a maker in a war era gets offered weapons contracts). Currently vx_ cards exist only for scholar+turning, soldier+war, maker+plenty. The solver/wanderer+plague, scholar+war, maker+hard etc. intersections are empty — those lives fall back into the generic adult pool.
improvements.why: The vocation system's best moments are the cross-cards. Expanding vx_ coverage to all 4 vocations × all 6 eras × some dynasty conditions would make the intersection space much richer and would directly serve structural variety across dynasties.

improvements.what: Replace the two single-option fate cards (f_grace, f_reversal) with binary or ternary choices that have genuinely different downstream effects. f_grace could offer: 'take it and be changed' (spirit+heart) vs. 'take it and feel undeserving' (spirit only, remember 'received_grace' that later gates a callback about paying it forward or failing to). f_reversal could offer: 'retrench immediately' vs. 'borrow time and keep going' (flagging peril). No-choice events read as filler in a choice-driven game.
improvements.why: The fate events are meant to be 'things that simply happen' for tone — but a choice of how to respond is still a character-defining moment. Adding a response choice preserves the surprise of the external event while making the player's reaction matter.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 new 'elder cap' cards for the childless-with-spouse path and the solitary-and-distinguished path (e.g., a solitary life with high mind gets a specific elder card about leaving behind a body of work, not just e_solitary's generic 'count what the solitude built'). Currently the e_childless card is excellent but fires only on the married-without-children shape; a solitary elder who built a career (high means + mind, no love) has no vocation-specific cap — they get the generic elder pool, which by gen 3 is noticeably thin.
improvements.why: The solitary and childless shapes are the freshest structural additions, but their elder sections don't yet match the richness of the domestic shape's elder arc. A variety-seeker who specifically chooses a solitary vocation-driven life will notice the elder section feels generic.

improvements.what: Introduce 1-2 late-dynasty 'house memory' events that can only fire when the dynasty is 4+ generations deep and the house has reached a specific reputation peak — moments where the ACCUMULATED CHARACTER of the house confronts the current life directly, not just via d_motto_test. For example: a scholarly house at gen 5 could get a card where a foreign institution wants to name something after the family, forcing a choice about whether to accept the institutionalisation of the family name. This would make long-dynasty play feel qualitatively different from early-dynasty play.
improvements.why: The dynasty layer's payoff currently plateaus after the motto crystallises (usually gen 2-3). There is no new dynasty-layer content that could only arrive at gen 5+. A variety-seeker playing a long dynasty will exhaust the dynasty novelty around gen 3 and coast.

verdict: A genuinely varied and often fresh literary life-sim with real structural divergence from vocations, eras, and dynasty memory — but a variety-seeker will notice the childhood checklist, the marriage/child obligation beat, the thinning onceDyn pool in long dynasties, and the uniform grammar of its 'competing goods' moments before dynasty 6, keeping it below the 8 threshold.
